title: Sector Overview #1 | Luxury Goods | October 2026
author: Alexis Rondeaux
summary: The luxury market is stabilising, not recovering: Q3 2026 broke the recovery narrative as China's tax crackdown hit the top cohort, hard luxury outgrew fashion, and sector leaders now trade at decade-low multiples.
key_takeaways: Market size: personal luxury goods worth €358bn in 2025; Bain base case of +2% to +4% market growth in 2026
Q3 2026 sales, year on year: LVMH Fashion & Leather Goods -5% (organic), Gucci -6% (comparable), Hermès +4.3% (constant FX, its slowest quarter since early 2020)
China: sales of the top 25 luxury brands fell more than 10% year on year in July 2026
Hard luxury: Richemont jewellery sales +24% at constant FX in Q1 FY27 (quarter to June 2026)
Share prices: LVMH, Hermès and Kering down about 40% year to date; LVMH valued at about 16x forward earnings (P/E), its lowest in more than ten years
disclaimer: Student research for educational purposes only. Not investment advice.
